e-4768.knowledge_point: Finding the LU Factorization Using a Single Elementary Row Operation
e-4768.problem:
Given that
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14062432/assets/d4fa85cab74f4bda57059d1c6abc9dacea665531ce84ba9d2f1598a13c49ef60.png) 
has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then $L=$
e-4768.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 6 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{2} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since $E_1A=U,$ we can invert $E_1$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

e-4769.knowledge_point: Finding the Lower Triangular Matrix Given the Elementary Row Operations
e-4769.problem:
Suppose that a $3 \times 3$ matrix $F$ is reduced to row echelon form using the following elementary row operations, applied in the order in which they appear:

$$
R_2:=R_2+R_1, \qquad
	R_3:=R_3+2R_1
$$

Given that $F$ has the LU factorization $F=LU,$ then $L=$
e-4769.worked_solution:
Applying $R_2:=R_2 + {\color{red}1} \cdot R_1$ and then $R_3:=R_3+ {\color{red}2} \cdot R_1$ is equivalent to multiplying $F$ from the left by the following elementary matrices:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14062432/assets/5eb696ca679a0079e8460d472b6f172df4f2e29f5dfef6cbdee388c55dcb1db5.png)

Now, since $E_2E_1F=U,$ we can invert $E_2$ and $E_1$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}F & =U \\ {E}_{1}F & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ F & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ F & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ F & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ F & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}\cdot U\end{aligned}
$$

e-4770.problem:
Given that

e-4770.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 8 & 0 \\ 5 & 11 & -6 \\ 0 & -4 & 16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{5}{4}){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -\frac{5}{4} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 8 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & -4 & 16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{2} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 8 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & -8\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since $E_2E_1A=U,$ we can invert $E_2$ and $E_1$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ {E}_{1}A & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -\frac{5}{4} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ \frac{5}{4} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ \frac{5}{4} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}4 & 8 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & -8\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Given that 
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 6 & 9 & -8\end{aligned}]$
has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then $L=$
after.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 6 & 9 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the LU Factorization Using a Single Elementary Row Operation
content.problem:
Given that 
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 6 & 9 & -8\end{aligned}]$
has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then $L=$
content.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 6 & 9 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Given that 
$A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -1 \\ -6 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]$
has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then $L=$
after.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -1 \\ -6 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

To find the matrices L and U, we reduce the matrix A to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to A in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

A=[32−1−6−2300−1]R2:=R2+2R1⟺[100210001]⏞E1⋅A∼[32−102100−1]=U

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix U. Now, since E1A=U, we can invert E1 to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

E1A=UA=E1−1UA=[100210001]−1UA=[100−210001]⏟L[32−102100−1]⏟U.

content.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -1 \\ -6 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Given that 
$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 7 & 0 \\ 4 & 9 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}]$
has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then $L=$
after.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 7 & 0 \\ 4 & 9 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 7 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}4 & 7 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the LU Factorization Using a Single Elementary Row Operation
content.problem:
Given that 
$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 7 & 0 \\ 4 & 9 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}]$
has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then $L=$
content.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 7 & 0 \\ 4 & 9 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 7 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}4 & 7 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Given that
$A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]$
has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then ${l}_{32}\cdot {u}_{33}=$
after.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}

content.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${l}_{32}=-\frac{1}{2},{u}_{33}=3,$ and ${l}_{32}\cdot {u}_{33}=-\frac{3}{2}.$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Given that
$A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 6 & 2 \\ 12 & 16 & -5\end{aligned}]$
has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then $L=$
after.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 6 & 2 \\ 12 & 16 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 6 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -9\end{aligned}] \\  & =U.\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 6 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 6 & 2 \\ 12 & 16 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 6 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -9\end{aligned}] \\  & =U.\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 6 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: If E₂E₁C=U, then C=E₁⁻¹E₂⁻¹U. Reversing the row operations adds 3R₁ to row 2 and subtracts 3R₁ from row 3. Thus L has entries 3 at (2,1) and −3 at (3,1), giving option c.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Suppose that a $3\times 3$ matrix $C$ is reduced to row echelon form using the following elementary row operations, applied in the order in which they appear:

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1},\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1}
$$

Given that $C$ has the LU factorization $C=LU,$ then $L=$
after.worked_solution:
Applying ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{1}$ and then ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3\cdot {R}_{1}$ is equivalent to multiplying $C$ from the left by the following elementary matrices:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{1}}\cdot C=U
$$

Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}C=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}C & =U \\ {E}_{1}C & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ C & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ C & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ C & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ C & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}\cdot U\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Lower Triangular Matrix Given the Elementary Row Operations
content.problem:
Suppose that a $3\times 3$ matrix $C$ is reduced to row echelon form using the following elementary row operations, applied in the order in which they appear:

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1},\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1}
$$

Given that $C$ has the LU factorization $C=LU,$ then $L=$
content.worked_solution:
Applying ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{1}$ and then ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3\cdot {R}_{1}$ is equivalent to multiplying $C$ from the left by the following elementary matrices:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{1}}\cdot C=U
$$

Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}C=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}C & =U \\ {E}_{1}C & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ C & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ C & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ C & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ C & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}\cdot U\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
Suppose that a $3\times 3$ matrix $H$ is reduced to row echelon form using the following elementary row operations, applied in the order in which they appear:

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1},\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-4{R}_{1}.
$$

Given that $H$ has the LU factorization $H=LU,$ then $L=$
after.worked_solution:
Applying ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4\cdot {R}_{1}$ and then ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-4)\cdot {R}_{1}$ is equivalent to multiplying $H$ from the left by the following elementary matrices:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{1}}\cdot H=U
$$

Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}H=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}H & =U \\ {E}_{1}H & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ H & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ H & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ H & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ H & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}\cdot U\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Lower Triangular Matrix Given the Elementary Row Operations
content.problem:
Suppose that a $3\times 3$ matrix $H$ is reduced to row echelon form using the following elementary row operations, applied in the order in which they appear:

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1},\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-4{R}_{1}.
$$

Given that $H$ has the LU factorization $H=LU,$ then $L=$
content.worked_solution:
Applying ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4\cdot {R}_{1}$ and then ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-4)\cdot {R}_{1}$ is equivalent to multiplying $H$ from the left by the following elementary matrices:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{1}}\cdot H=U
$$

Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}H=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}H & =U \\ {E}_{1}H & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ H & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ H & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ H & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ H & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}\cdot U\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Since E₂E₁C=U, L=E₁⁻¹E₂⁻¹. The inverse operations add R₁ to row 2 and subtract 4R₁ from row 3. Their product has entries 1 at (2,1) and −4 at (3,1), giving option d.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
Suppose that a $3\times 3$ matrix $C$ is reduced to row echelon form using the following elementary row operations, applied in the order in which they appear:

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-{R}_{1},\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1}
$$

Given that $C$ has the LU factorization $C=LU,$ then $L=$
after.worked_solution:
Applying ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{1}$ and then ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+4\cdot {R}_{1}$ is equivalent to multiplying $C$ from the left by the following elementary matrices:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{1}}\cdot C=U
$$

Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}C=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}C & =U \\ {E}_{1}C & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ C & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ C & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ C & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ C & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}\cdot U\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Lower Triangular Matrix Given the Elementary Row Operations
content.problem:
Suppose that a $3\times 3$ matrix $C$ is reduced to row echelon form using the following elementary row operations, applied in the order in which they appear:

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-{R}_{1},\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1}
$$

Given that $C$ has the LU factorization $C=LU,$ then $L=$
content.worked_solution:
Applying ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{1}$ and then ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+4\cdot {R}_{1}$ is equivalent to multiplying $C$ from the left by the following elementary matrices:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{1}}\cdot C=U
$$

Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}C=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}C & =U \\ {E}_{1}C & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ C & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ C & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ C & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ C & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}\cdot U\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Applying ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{1}$ and then ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{1}$ is equivalent to multiplying $H$ from the left by the following elementary matrices:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{1}}\cdot H=U
$$

Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}H=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}H & =U \\ {E}_{1}H & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ H & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ H & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ H & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ H & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}\cdot U\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
Suppose that a $3\times 3$ matrix $C$ is reduced to row echelon form using the following elementary row operations, applied in the order in which they appear:

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1},\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+9{R}_{1}
$$

Given that $C$ has the LU factorization $C=LU,$ then $L=$
after.worked_solution:
Applying ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+1\cdot {R}_{1}$ and then ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+9\cdot {R}_{1}$ is equivalent to multiplying $C$ from the left by the following elementary matrices:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 9 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{1}}\cdot C=U
$$

Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}C=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}C & =U \\ {E}_{1}C & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ C & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ C & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 9 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ C & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -9 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ C & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ -9 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}\cdot U\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Lower Triangular Matrix Given the Elementary Row Operations
content.problem:
Suppose that a $3\times 3$ matrix $C$ is reduced to row echelon form using the following elementary row operations, applied in the order in which they appear:

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1},\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+9{R}_{1}
$$

Given that $C$ has the LU factorization $C=LU,$ then $L=$
content.worked_solution:
Applying ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+1\cdot {R}_{1}$ and then ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+9\cdot {R}_{1}$ is equivalent to multiplying $C$ from the left by the following elementary matrices:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 9 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{1}}\cdot C=U
$$

Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}C=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}C & =U \\ {E}_{1}C & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ C & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ C & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 9 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ C & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -9 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ C & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ -9 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}\cdot U\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 11
after.problem:
Given that 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]$ has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then $L=$
after.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ {E}_{1}A & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Given that 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]$ has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then $L=$
content.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ {E}_{1}A & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
Given that 
$A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 5 & 1 & -8 \\ -4 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]$ has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then ${l}_{31}\cdot {u}_{23}=$
after.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 5 & 1 & -8 \\ -4 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+5{R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ -4 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ {E}_{1}A & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${l}_{31}=4,{u}_{23}=2,$ and ${l}_{31}\cdot {u}_{23}=8.$

$A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 5 & 1 & -8 \\ -4 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]$ has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then ${l}_{31}\cdot {u}_{23}=$
content.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 5 & 1 & -8 \\ -4 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+5{R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ -4 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ {E}_{1}A & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${l}_{31}=4,{u}_{23}=2,$ and ${l}_{31}\cdot {u}_{23}=8.$

decision.explanation: Apply R₂ ← R₂ − 4R₁ and R₃ ← R₃ + 3R₁, obtaining rows (0,3,1) and (0,−6,1). Thus l₃₂=−6/3=−2. Applying R₃ ← R₃ + 2R₂ gives u₃₃=3, so l₃₂u₃₃=−6.

after.problem:
Given that 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 4 & -5 & 9 \\ -3 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}]$ has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then ${l}_{32}\cdot {u}_{33}=$
after.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 4 & -5 & 9 \\ -3 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ -3 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & -6 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{3}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{2}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{3}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{3},$ ${E}_{2},$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{3}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ {E}_{2}{E}_{1}A & ={E}_{3}^{-1}U \\ {E}_{1}A & ={E}_{2}^{-1}{E}_{3}^{-1}U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}{E}_{3}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${l}_{32}=-2,$ ${u}_{33}=3,$ and ${l}_{32}\cdot {u}_{33}=-6.$

content.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 4 & -5 & 9 \\ -3 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ -3 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & -6 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{3}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{2}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{3}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{3},$ ${E}_{2},$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{3}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ {E}_{2}{E}_{1}A & ={E}_{3}^{-1}U \\ {E}_{1}A & ={E}_{2}^{-1}{E}_{3}^{-1}U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}{E}_{3}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}

after.name: Question 15
after.problem:
Given that 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}]$ has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then $L=$
after.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ {E}_{1}A & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the LU Factorization Using Two or More Elementary Row Operations
content.problem:
Given that 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}]$ has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then $L=$
content.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ {E}_{1}A & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$
